protocol_chronology.amendment_reason: Structured transformations may reactivate parameter aliases with identical current BAM state; the guaranteed hierarchy therefore uses parameter-world identity as the finest target.

main_findings: The parameter-world to exact-counterfactual to binary-decision target hierarchy held with zero violations in both W0 and W1.

Current BAM-state identity is not a sufficient generic surrogate for future-response identity: one W1 climate fiber had a single current A/B/M/tau state but split into two exact and binary climate responses.
Decision without parameter-world identification was common for all three structured transformations in both universes.
Expanding the admissible ecological world family removed real decision certificates for all three transformations: 10 climate, 105 biotic-stress and 44 barrier-restoration truth cases.
Many decision certificates nevertheless survived W1: 636 climate, 498 biotic-stress and 700 barrier-restoration truth cases despite zero parameter-world-identified W1 truths.

Biotic-stress decisions were most sensitive to W0-to-W1 universe expansion in this frozen synthetic design, retaining 82.6 percent of W0 binary certificates versus 98.5 percent for climate and 94.1 percent for barrier restoration.
claim_boundary: The climate, biotic-stress and barrier-restoration operators are synthetic transformations, not calibrated management or climate scenarios.
Current-state-identical parameter worlds can respond differently only because the transformation depends on latent parameter semantics not fully captured by the current BAM-state projection.
Counts are conditional on the frozen 12 systems, W0/W1 world families and transformation definitions.
The results do not imply that parameter identity is generally required for robust ecological decisions.
The results do not alter the frozen BAM inverse-identifiability manuscript or EOG-WF empirical programme.
